Inspect corrected selection-sampler counters

Source: R/selection-cache.R
selection_sampler_info.Rd

Reports the work of the corrected selection sampler: the record of a fitted model, or the counters of the current R process.

Usage

selection_sampler_info(clear = FALSE, fit = NULL)

Arguments

clear

reset the process counters before reporting them. Cannot be combined with fit.

fit

a fitted selection model (for example from bselmodel.mv() or RoBMA.mv()) whose record to report, or NULL for the process counters.

Value

Without fit, a data frame with proposal, acceptance and correction-rejection counts, and an acceptance rate (NA before any proposals). With fit, a one-row data frame with the record described in details; a fit without a record (not a selection model, or fitted before the record existed) gives NA counts and complete = FALSE.

Details

The corrected sampler is the default, RoBMA.options(selection.sampler = "slice.coarse"); set selection.sampler = "slice" before fitting to use the other samplers instead, or "jags.default" for only the samplers JAGS assigns. The selection-weight parameters of a branch of a publication-bias mixture that sampler.gates declares are updated together by the corrected gated block sampler when one of the branch's selection blocks takes part (below); other gated parameters (PET and PEESE slopes, and weights whose selection blocks do not take part) keep the gated sampler of the BayesTools JAGS module. A block that sampler.blocks declares (see RoBMA.options) is updated by the corrected block sampler when one of its selection blocks takes part (below), and by the factor slice sampler of the BayesTools JAGS module otherwise. A scalar indicator (the bias indicator, the heterogeneity inclusion indicator and effect and moderator indicators with fixed prior probabilities) with such a selection block among its children is updated by the screened indicator sampler, unless a joint sampler updates it or sampler.probabilities records its conditional probabilities. Independent step-selection rows (the estimates of RoBMA() and the single-estimate clusters of RoBMA.mv()) take part in the gated weights and the bias indicator through a row cache (below). Every proposal is corrected against the full original likelihood and prior. Only the selection normalizer used to construct proposals is coarsened. A reversible slice transition for that surrogate is followed by a Metropolis correction using both original and surrogate densities at the current and proposed states. The original likelihood keeps its existing numerical integration controls and diagnostics; the correction does not replace those numerical integrals by symbolic exact values.

Dense multivariate step blocks. The surrogate rounds means and the logarithms of positive weights to fixed grids. Each covariance diagonal is rounded upward on a grid whose origin is that row's squared original sampling SE; off-diagonal covariances, original SEs, selection cutoffs, and zero weights are retained. These are proposal grids, not changes to fitted variance components or the input covariance. The Gaussian numerator and observed weights use the actual parameters. At most the first selection.coarse_max_rules rules of the fitted quadrature schedule are tried, with its existing integration criterion. If a valid anchor cannot be constructed or its covariance-envelope calculation is unsupported or unsuccessful, its prescribed normalizer is one; the proposal stage does not fall back to QMC. This fallback is independent of cache history and memory capacity and remains subject to the full-target correction. It does not replace full-target integration failures.

Rank-one cluster and factor step blocks. The surrogate is the exact numerator (Gaussian log density and observed log weights at the actual parameters) minus the log normalizer of one rule of the block's own Gauss-Hermite schedule: rule number selection.coarse_max_rules, or the last rule of a shorter schedule, evaluated at the actual parameters. No grid rounding, change test, certificate, refinement, sparse grid, QMC or cache enters, so the surrogate is a deterministic function of the sampled state; the correction evaluates the exact block, which keeps its ordinary numerical controls and diagnostics. Where that rule is unavailable at an update (a best-weight rule in the current state, or a non-finite normalizer) the surrogate is the exact density of the block. A block takes part unless its fixed controls rule it out: a weight rule fixed at a best-weight rule, a kernel mode fixed at the normal kernel, or, for a factor block, a rule beyond the node budget at the declared rank (rank two to six at the default setting). In model-averaged fits the weight rule and the kernel mode are nodes of the bias indicator, so their blocks take part, with the exact density in the states of the indicator that have a best-weight rule. Blocks fixed at a best-weight rule, blocks of higher rank and blocks with a fixed normal kernel keep the ordinary sampler.

A scalar update is eligible when at least one stochastic child of the updated node is a dense multivariate block or a coarse-capable cluster or factor block; its other children enter the surrogate through their exact densities.

Step-selection rows. The weights of a branch whose estimates enter as independent step-selection rows, and an indicator that sets the weights or the kernel of such rows (the bias indicator), take part through a row cache: while only those weights or only the indicator move, the probabilities of each row's selection intervals are fixed, so they are computed once per update and each surrogate evaluation is a weighted sum and a logarithm per row. This is the rows' exact density up to rounding; a row whose mean moves with the indicator (the PET and PEESE branches), or whose normalizer is too small for the cached sum, enters with its exact density. A proposal is evidence for the cache (below) only when its surrogate and exact changes differ by more than a relative \(10^{-9}\). Indicators that change only the rows' means or variances (heterogeneity, effect and moderator indicators) keep their samplers.

Blocks. The corrected block sampler makes one factor slice sweep on the surrogate over all parameters of a declared block, in forward or backward direction order chosen at random at each update, and accepts or rejects the whole sweep with the same correction. The random order makes the proposal reversible, so the corrected chain targets the exact posterior of the block; the directions and widths adapt as in the factor slice sampler. Gamma parameters that enter the model only through their proportions (the Dirichlet weights of a heterogeneity allocation, the weights of a cumulative weight function) are updated through their proportions, and their sum is drawn from its gamma distribution at each update.

Gated weights. While its branch is inactive, the weights of a branch are drawn from their prior, as in the gated sampler; while it is active, they are updated by the corrected block sweep, whose directions adapt only on those updates.

Indicators. The screened indicator sampler scores every level of the indicator with the surrogates of its selection children, each level's score computed from that level's model state alone. At each update it proposes a level from these scores by one of two moves, chosen at random independently of the state: with probability 7/8 a Metropolized Gibbs step (a level other than the current one, accepted on the scores), with probability 1/8 a draw from the scores with the current level included (which keeps a thinned chain from alternating between two equally likely levels). A change of level is corrected with one Metropolis step against the exact scores of both levels, so the chain targets the exact posterior, and an update that keeps the current level costs no exact evaluation. Vector-valued and unrelated updates, and updates whose selection children are all without a coarse rule (other than the step-selection rows above), retain ordinary JAGS samplers. For any surrogate computed from the model state it scores, the corrected chain targets the exact full conditional; a coarser rule changes the acceptance rate and the cost, not the posterior.

Fallback. Each corrected sampler (one per parameter, block or indicator and chain) chooses its kernel once, at the end of adaptation, from its evidence proposals during adaptation: proposals for which at least one selection block evaluated a surrogate that differs from its exact density (none does under the normal kernel of a model-averaged fit's normal branches, or where its rule is unavailable); for an indicator, changes of level whose surrogate differed at either level. With selection.coarse_min_acceptance above 0 (default 0.90) it updates its parameter with the exact slice sampler (a block with the factor slice sweep of the exact posterior, an indicator by enumerating its levels) for the rest of the fit when it made at least 50 evidence proposals during adaptation and their acceptance rate is below the threshold. With fewer it stays corrected and the warning below judges it after adaptation. A sampler whose selection blocks can never differ from their exact densities (decided from the fixed settings of the blocks) is not created. A block of d directions is judged per direction: its acceptance rate to the power 1/d, here, for min_sampler_rate and for the warning below. Both kernels leave the posterior unchanged and the choice is not revisited, so the chain after adaptation is a single exact kernel. A threshold of 0 disables the fallback and the warning. Every model build (a fit, and each parallel worker's or extension's rebuild of the model) adapts and decides again.

Record. A fitted selection model keeps the record of its corrected samplers, collected from every process that ran chains and summed over the fit and its extensions (update()): sampler and min_acceptance, the settings the model was fitted with (sampler shows the value the fit was made with, so fits of earlier versions show "coarse_corrected" or "default"; min_acceptance is 0 for fits made before the threshold existed); samplers, the corrected sampler objects constructed, one per parameter, block or indicator and chain and counted again for every model build; fallback_samplers, those that switched to the exact kernel, and fallback_low_acceptance, the same count under the one remaining reason (records of development versions also split out two retired reasons, which are dropped); sampling_proposed and sampling_accepted, the evidence proposals made after adaptation by samplers that stayed corrected and the proposals whose correction accepted them (unchanged values included), counting burn-in and all sampling iterations through the end of each chain or extension, including iterations between retained draws when thinning; sampling_judged, the sum over the samplers of their proposals times their acceptance rate per direction (rate^(1/d) for a block of d parameters, the accepted proposals of a scalar sampler, over each backend run); acceptance_rate, the judged, per-direction rate sampling_judged / sampling_proposed, which equals the raw rate sampling_accepted / sampling_proposed for fits without blocks (NA without proposals); min_sampler_rate, the lowest acceptance rate of one sampler over one backend run (of the fit, of an automatic extension or of an update()), among samplers with at least 1,000 proposals in that run (NA when none has). A fit made of several backend runs (automatic or update() extensions) takes this minimum over more and shorter runs. While a sampler still makes at least 1,000 proposals in a run, such a fit reaches the warning more readily than one long run of the same model, and with fewer proposals per run it has no worst-sampler rate. In JASP, each sampling run contributes one report per process across all its progress ticks. The last element is complete, FALSE when part of the chain was drawn without a record (an extension of a fit saved before the record existed, a process whose report failed, or draws added without any report), in which case the counts cover the recorded part only. Adaptation updates, proposals that are not evidence (for example in the normal branches of a model average) and updates of samplers that fell back are not counted.

Warning. A fit or an extension whose record has at least 1,000 counted proposals and whose judged acceptance_rate, or min_sampler_rate, is below min_acceptance warns with the condition classes RoBMA_selection_sampler_low_acceptance and RoBMA_selection_sampler_warning: sampling is exact but inefficient. The message is kept with the fit's warnings, replaced at every extension.

Errors. An error of a corrected sampler, of the location block sampler or of its heterogeneity scale move names the node and ends with a hint, in most cases the option that returns the parameters to the ordinary samplers and a request to report the model; errors of the joint bias, Gaussian and cluster samplers end with the same hint (sampler.joint = "off"). Errors whose message contains a bracketed name are signalled with that name as condition class and the shared parent class RoBMA_sampler_error: RoBMA_location_untracked_mean (a mean of a likelihood node is not the one the location block's verified design predicts) and RoBMA_location_scale_invariance (the heterogeneity scale move changed a likelihood node, which it must leave unchanged). One error concerns the data or the chain's state instead: where a sampler evaluates the exact density of the state its chain is in and, after adaptation, the absolute log densities of the likelihood terms of that evaluation (the terms its move differences) sum to more than \(10^9\), it stops with the class RoBMA_likelihood_not_representable. At that state estimates lie far from the values the model gives them, and double precision cannot resolve the differences that the acceptance ratios need. The ordinary samplers return draws for such data without a warning; check the estimates and their standard errors, their units and the model. A chain can also reach such a state while other chains sample the same data; other initial values or a longer adaptation may then avoid it. While adapting, a chain that starts far from the data raises nothing.

Process counters. Without fit, the function reports the counters of all corrected samplers in this process (every proposal with a correction, evidence or not, and for an indicator every change of level), including adaptation; clear them between phases for a sampling-only comparison. They do not report separate parallel workers. Inspect them between sampling calls.

Already compiled samplers retain their grid, coarse rule-budget and threshold settings. Coarse settings can affect sampling efficiency even when correction acceptance is high. Compare effective samples per second for parameters of interest, not only iteration times or this acceptance rate.
